conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion**  
Yes, clinical evidence supports that whole-body vibration (WBV) therapy is effective as a complementary intervention to help prevent bone fractures in people with osteoporosis.

**Key Evidence**
* **Fracture and Fall Prevention:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses indicate that WBV exercise significantly lowers fall rates and overall fracture risk among older adults, making it a safe supplementary strategy for osteoporosis management (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6027066/, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139).
* **Bone Loss Reduction:** WBV applies cyclic mechanical stress that regulates bone metabolism. Clinical studies show low-magnitude vibration reduces bone loss in critical areas like the lumbar spine and improves bone mineral density (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/endocrinology/articles/10.3389/fendo.2025.1611677/full, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13018-016-0357-2).
* **Accessible Exercise Alternative:** WBV serves as a practical therapy for individuals unable to engage in high-impact exercise, helping maintain skeletal integrity and balance.

**Sources**
* https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6027066/
* https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139
* https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/endocrinology/articles/10.3389/fendo.2025.1611677/full
* https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13018-016-0357-2
